answer.rationale: Memory_73 (promotional pricing) is weakly supported for sustainable long-term qualified revenue because it addresses acquisition lift but omits critical data on long-term retention, unit economics, and margin impact. Aggressive promotional pricing can create cohorts of price-sensitive customers with higher churn and lower lifetime value, directly conflicting with sustainability. Memory_44 (enterprise sales-assisted flows) is strongly supported because pipeline quality correlates with conversion rates, deal size, and retention—all core to sustainable revenue. Memory_31, memory_86, and memory_91 are well-supported as they improve activation and time-to-value, which drive retention and reduce churn. Memory_57 is moderately well-supported; referral incentives add qualified revenue without harming retention, but lacks data on margin, acquisition cost, and long-term cohort economics. The omission of retention/churn data in memory_73 combined with its focus on price competition makes it the least aligned with sustainable long-term qualified revenue in the current context where competitor pricing pressure is occurring.
